name: Saturate drums without losing punch: an envelope follower reads the clean signal on a muted parallel chain, and its output drives a gain stage placed after the saturator so the saturated signal's peaks are pushed back up and its dynamic range is restored
goal: Add saturation warmth to drums (or a melody loop) while keeping their punch: because saturation shaves peaks and flattens dynamic range, measure the dry signal's envelope on a muted parallel chain and use it to modulate a gain stage after the saturator, so loud hits get louder again. Delta vs our saturation variants: envelope-follower-driven gain restoration after the saturator.
prerequisites: DAW with an envelope follower / peak controller that can modulate a parameter
Any saturator and a gain/utility device

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: Drum bus or loop that loses punch when saturated

constraints: Original synthesis/processing recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any DAW/synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks, impulse responses or samples copied.
Only gain is modulated after the saturator; nothing else in that chain.
Values (base/depth) are set by ear; the source quotes about 30-40% base and 60-70% amount on its follower.
Original routing recipe; the free patch offered in the source is not needed.
Drums early (Matt's taste): if the track has drums, the kick/drum loop enters by about count 8 (roughly 10-12 s), with only the pad before that.

steps.action: Saturate the drums and watch the waveform: peaks get shaved and the drums stop hitting in the mix.
steps.expect: Problem confirmed: warmth but lost punch

steps.action: Build two parallel chains: chain A holds only an envelope follower/peak controller and is muted (it just measures); chain B holds the saturator followed by a gain/utility device.
Map the follower's output to the gain device in chain B.
steps.expect: Gain rises with each dry peak

steps.action: Set the follower base around 30-40% and the amount around 60-70%, then adjust until saturated hits match the original punch.
Compare in the mix; for melodic loops combine with sidechain ducking to the drum loop for pump.

verification: Peak-to-RMS (crest factor) of the processed drums is close to the dry drums while harmonics are added.
